## AI-Generated Fix (php)

```php
<?php

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::get('/.env', function () {
    abort(404);
});

// Alternatively, ensure the web server configuration blocks access to .env files.
// For Apache, add the following to your .htaccess file:
// <Files .env>
//     Order allow,deny
//     Deny from all
// </Files>

// For Nginx, add the following to your server block:
// location ~* \.env {
//     deny all;
// }

```

---

## Explanation

The .env file was accessible publicly, exposing sensitive information. The fix involves adding a route in Laravel to return a 404 error for requests to the .env file, preventing unauthorized access. Additionally, web server configurations for Apache and Nginx are provided to block access to .env files at the server level, enhancing security.
